title: Character Name Origins: Where Gandalf Came From
description: A wizard's name, an Old Norse list, and a draft where everyone wore someone else's name—five steps into Tolkien's borrowings.

questions.question: Tolkien took the wizard Gandalf's name from an Old Norse list of what kind of creatures?
questions.explanation: In the Norse original, 'Gandálfr' means something like 'wand-elf'—and he's listed among the dwarves, not the wizards.

questions.question: That list of dwarves sits inside Völuspá, the opening poem of which Old Norse collection?
questions.explanation: The 'Dvergatal' (tally of dwarves) in the Poetic Edda supplied Dwalin, Balin, Kili, Fili, Bombur, Thorin—nearly the whole company in The Hobbit.

questions.question: The same Poetic Edda list gave Thorin his surname, translated from 'Eikinskjaldi'—what is it?
questions.explanation: In the poem Eikinskjaldi is a separate dwarf. Tolkien invented the story of Thorin using an oak branch as a shield.

questions.question: In Tolkien's early drafts, the dwarf leader we know as Thorin Oakenshield was named what?
questions.explanation: A note on an early draft reads: "Gandalf was originally chief Dwarf (= Thorin)." True to the Edda, the name started out on a dwarf.

questions.question: With the name Gandalf going to a dwarf in those drafts, what was the wizard originally called?
questions.explanation: Bladorthin survives as a dead king mentioned once in The Hobbit—the only trace of the wizard's first name.
